items.text: If we had invested in cloud storage two years ago, we ___ not have this capacity problem now.

ok.de: Vergangene Ursache, heutige Folge: if + Past Perfect, would + Grundform.
ok.en: A past cause with a result today: if + past perfect, would + base form.

wrong.de: will steht nicht in dieser unwirklichen Aussage über heute.
wrong.en: will does not fit this unreal statement about today.

wrong.de: had not have gibt es nicht; im Hauptsatz steht would not have.
wrong.en: had not have does not exist; the main clause takes would not have.

wrong.de: did not have beschreibt keine unwirkliche Folge.
wrong.en: did not have does not describe an unreal result.

items.text: If I were better at math, I ___ have chosen a different career years ago, and I would earn more now.

ok.de: Heutiger Zustand, frühere Folge: if + Past Simple, would have + Partizip.
ok.en: A present state with an earlier result: if + past simple, would have + participle.

wrong.de: will have passt nicht zu einer unwirklichen Bedingung.
wrong.en: will have does not fit an unreal condition.

wrong.de: had have gibt es nicht; im Hauptsatz steht would have + Partizip.
wrong.en: had have does not exist; the main clause takes would have + participle.

wrong.de: did have drückt keine unwirkliche Folge aus.
wrong.en: did have does not express an unreal result.

items.text: I wish we ___ more storage space; the current server is full again, and it is only the middle of the month.

ok.de: Wunsch über die Gegenwart: wish + Past Simple (had).
ok.en: A wish about the present: wish + past simple (had).

wrong.de: wish + have gibt es nicht; für Wünsche über heute braucht wish die Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: wish + have does not exist; wishes about now need wish + past.

wrong.de: wish we has ist falsch.
wrong.en: wish we has is wrong.

wrong.de: wish + would drückt Ärger über Verhalten aus, nicht den Wunsch nach Besitz.
wrong.en: wish + would expresses annoyance at behavior, not a wish to own something.

items.text: I wish it ___ already Friday; this week has been exhausting, and I have another long meeting tomorrow.

ok.de: Wunsch über jetzt: wish + Vergangenheit (it were/was Friday).
ok.en: A wish about now: wish + past (it were/was Friday).

wrong.de: wish + is gibt es nicht; wish braucht die Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: wish + is does not exist; wish needs the past.

wrong.de: wish + be gibt es nicht.
wrong.en: wish + be does not exist.

wrong.de: wish + would passt nicht zu einem Zustand wie „es ist Freitag“.
wrong.en: wish + would does not fit a state like “it is Friday”.

items.text: I wish I ___ asked for a written confirmation before sending the goods, because now the customer denies everything.

ok.de: Bedauern über die Vergangenheit: wish + Past Perfect (had asked).
ok.en: Regret about the past: wish + past perfect (had asked).

wrong.de: wish + have asked gibt es nicht; für Bedauern über früher braucht wish had + Partizip.
wrong.en: wish + have asked does not exist; regret about the past needs wish + had + participle.

wrong.de: wish + would asked gibt es nicht.
wrong.en: wish + would asked does not exist.

wrong.de: wish + did asked ist falsch.
wrong.en: wish + did asked is wrong.

items.text: She wishes she ___ not signed the contract without reading the small print, but now it is too late.

ok.de: Bedauern: wish + had (not) + Partizip.
ok.en: Regret: wish + had (not) + participle.

wrong.de: wishes she has not signed gibt es nicht; es braucht had not signed.
wrong.en: wishes she has not signed does not exist; it needs had not signed.

wrong.de: wishes she would not signed gibt es nicht.
wrong.en: wishes she would not signed does not exist.

wrong.de: wishes she did not signed ist falsch.
wrong.en: wishes she did not signed is wrong.

items.text: I wish the client ___ stop changing the requirements every other day; we can never finish anything.

ok.de: Ärger über wiederholtes Verhalten anderer: wish + would + Grundform.
ok.en: Annoyance at other people's repeated behavior: wish + would + base form.

wrong.de: wish + will gibt es nicht; für Ärger über Verhalten steht wish + would.
wrong.en: wish + will does not exist; annoyance at behavior takes wish + would.

wrong.de: wish + had stop gibt es nicht; had braucht ein Partizip (stopped).
wrong.en: wish + had stop does not exist; had needs a participle (stopped).

wrong.de: wish + did stop ist falsch.
wrong.en: wish + did stop is wrong.

items.text: I wish you ___ not leave your coffee cups all over the meeting room; it looks terrible every afternoon.

ok.de: Ärger über Gewohnheiten: wish + would (not) + Grundform.
ok.en: Annoyance at habits: wish + would (not) + base form.

wrong.de: wish you will not leave ist falsch; hier steht wish + would.
wrong.en: wish you will not leave is wrong; here it is wish + would.

wrong.de: wish you did not leave wäre Wunsch über einen Zustand, nicht über künftiges Verhalten.
wrong.en: wish you did not leave would be a wish about a state, not about future behavior.

wrong.de: wish you had not leave ist falsch.
wrong.en: wish you had not leave is wrong.

items.text: ___ I known about the delay, I would have informed the client immediately instead of letting him find out.

ok.de: Förmlich ohne if: Had + Subjekt + Partizip, would have …
ok.en: Formal without if: Had + subject + participle, would have …

wrong.de: Have I known gibt es hier nicht; die Umstellung der dritten Bedingung beginnt mit Had.
wrong.en: Have I known does not fit; the inverted third conditional starts with Had.

wrong.de: Did I known ist falsch.
wrong.en: Did I known is wrong.

wrong.de: Would I known ist falsch.
wrong.en: Would I known is wrong.

items.text: ___ I in your position, I would not accept the offer without negotiating the payment terms first.

ok.de: Förmlich ohne if: Were + Subjekt …, would … (= If I were in your position).
ok.en: Formal without if: Were + subject …, would … (= If I were in your position).

wrong.de: Was I in your position gibt es in dieser förmlichen Umstellung nicht.
wrong.en: Was I in your position does not exist in this formal inversion.

wrong.de: Am I in your position wäre eine Frage.
wrong.en: Am I in your position would be a question.

wrong.de: Be I in your position ist veraltet.
wrong.en: Be I in your position is archaic.

items.text: How long ___ you known the client, and did you ever work with his predecessor?

ok.de: know ist ein Zustandsverb: have known (nie have been knowing).
ok.en: know is a state verb: have known (never have been knowing).

wrong.de: How long are you known wäre Passiv und falsch gebaut.
wrong.en: How long are you known would be a badly built passive.

wrong.de: How long did you known ist falsch; nach did steht die Grundform.
wrong.en: How long did you known is wrong; after did comes the base form.

wrong.de: How long do you known ist falsch.
wrong.en: How long do you known is wrong.

items.text: I ___ known my neighbor since university, so I trust his judgment about anything related to property.

ok.de: Zustand bis jetzt mit since: have known (Present Perfect, keine -ing-Form).
ok.en: A state up to now with since: have known (present perfect, no -ing form).

wrong.de: I am known bedeutet „ich bin bekannt“ und ist Passiv.
wrong.en: I am known means “I am famous” and is passive.

wrong.de: I was known wäre Passiv in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: I was known would be passive in the past.

wrong.de: had known passt zu einer früheren Zeit, hier gilt es bis heute.
wrong.en: had known fits an earlier time, but this reaches up to now.

items.text: How ___ emails have you written since this morning, and have you replied to the customers?

ok.de: Zahl als Ergebnis fragt man mit How many + have written (einfache Form).
ok.en: A number as the result is asked with How many + have written (simple form).

wrong.de: much steht bei nicht zählbaren Dingen; emails sind zählbar.
wrong.en: much goes with uncountable things; emails are countable.

wrong.de: How long fragt nach der Dauer, nicht nach der Zahl.
wrong.en: How long asks about duration, not about number.

wrong.de: How often fragt nach der Häufigkeit.
wrong.en: How often asks about frequency.

items.text: How ___ have you been waiting for the technician, and did anyone give you an estimated time?

ok.de: Dauer bis jetzt: How long + have you been + -ing.
ok.en: Duration up to now: How long + have you been + -ing.

wrong.de: How many fragt nach einer Zahl; hier geht es um die Dauer.
wrong.en: How many asks for a number; this is about duration.

wrong.de: How much fragt nach einer Menge.
wrong.en: How much asks for an amount.

wrong.de: How often fragt nach der Häufigkeit, nicht nach der Dauer.
wrong.en: How often asks about frequency, not duration.

items.text: She ___ not belong to the sales team anymore; she moved to the finance department last month.

ok.de: belong ist ein Zustandsverb: Present Simple, Verneinung does not belong.
ok.en: belong is a state verb: present simple, negative does not belong.

wrong.de: do passt zu I, you, we, they; she verlangt does.
wrong.en: do goes with I, you, we, they; she needs does.

wrong.de: is not belong ist keine Form.
wrong.en: is not belong is not a form.

wrong.de: has not belong ist keine Form; belong braucht die Grundform.
wrong.en: has not belong is not a form; belong needs the base form.

items.text: We ___ thinking about moving the whole archive to a new data center next year, but nothing is decided yet.

ok.de: think im Sinn von „überlegen“ ist eine Handlung: are thinking.
ok.en: think meaning “consider” is an action: are thinking.

wrong.de: do thinking gibt es nicht; vor -ing steht eine Form von be.
wrong.en: do thinking does not exist; -ing needs a form of be.

wrong.de: have thinking ist keine Form.
wrong.en: have thinking is not a form.

wrong.de: will thinking ist keine Form; will braucht die Grundform.
wrong.en: will thinking is not a form; will needs the base form.

items.text: The conference starts ___ Tuesday at nine and ends on Friday afternoon, so we should book the hotel soon.

ok.de: Wochentage mit on: starts on Tuesday (Fahrplan im Present Simple).
ok.en: Weekdays take on: starts on Tuesday (a timetable in the present simple).

wrong.de: in steht vor Monaten und Jahren, nicht vor Wochentagen.
wrong.en: in goes before months and years, not weekdays.

wrong.de: at steht vor Uhrzeiten und Punkten wie at night.
wrong.en: at goes before clock times and points like at night.

wrong.de: by heißt „spätestens“, die Konferenz beginnt aber genau an diesem Tag.
wrong.en: by means “no later than”, but the conference begins on that day.

items.text: I will call you as soon ___ I land in Frankfurt, so please keep your phone nearby this evening.

ok.de: as soon as + Gegenwart (I land), im Hauptsatz will.
ok.en: as soon as + present (I land), will in the main clause.

wrong.de: as soon so gibt es nicht; die Wendung heißt as soon as.
wrong.en: as soon so does not exist; the phrase is as soon as.

wrong.de: as soon at gibt es nicht.
wrong.en: as soon at does not exist.

wrong.de: as soon how gibt es nicht.
wrong.en: as soon how does not exist.

items.text: ___ I send you the updated figures right now, or would you prefer to have them tomorrow morning?

ok.de: Angebot und Vorschlag: Shall I … ? oder Should I … ?
ok.en: An offer or suggestion: Shall I … ? or Should I … ?

wrong.de: Will I send you klingt wie eine Frage nach der Zukunft, nicht wie ein Angebot.
wrong.en: Will I send you sounds like a question about the future, not like an offer.

wrong.de: Do I send you fragt eher nach einer Regel als nach einem Angebot.
wrong.en: Do I send you asks about a rule more than it offers help.

wrong.de: Am I send you ist keine Form.
wrong.en: Am I send you is not a form.

items.text: Look at the sky: it ___ going to rain, so let us take the car instead of walking to the station.

ok.de: Vorhersage mit sichtbarem Zeichen: is going to + Grundform.
ok.en: A prediction based on what you can see: is going to + base form.

wrong.de: will + going to kann man nicht verbinden.
wrong.en: will and going to cannot be combined.

wrong.de: does going to gibt es nicht.
wrong.en: does going to does not exist.

wrong.de: has going to ist falsch; die Form lautet be going to.
wrong.en: has going to is wrong; the form is be going to.

items.text: We ___ going to launch the new product in May, but the supplier delayed everything by six weeks.

ok.de: Geplatzter Plan: was/were going to + Grundform; zu we gehört were.
ok.en: A plan that fell through: was/were going to + base form; we goes with were.

wrong.de: are going to ist Gegenwart; der Plan ist aber geplatzt (delayed).
wrong.en: are going to is present, but the plan has fallen through (delayed).

wrong.de: was passt zu I, he, she, it; zu we gehört were.
wrong.en: was goes with I, he, she, it; we needs were.

wrong.de: will launch ist Zukunft; gemeint ist ein Plan in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: will launch is future; a plan in the past is meant.

items.text: When I was a student, I ___ spend hours in the library every evening and read until it closed.

ok.de: Wiederholte Handlungen in der Vergangenheit: would + Grundform.
ok.en: Repeated actions in the past: would + base form.

wrong.de: used spend gibt es nicht; es heißt used to spend.
wrong.en: used spend does not exist; it is used to spend.

wrong.de: did spend wäre betont und einmalig, nicht „jeden Abend“.
wrong.en: did spend would be emphatic and one-off, not “every evening”.

wrong.de: was spend gibt es nicht.
wrong.en: was spend does not exist.

items.text: There ___ to be a small café on this corner, but it closed last year and now it is a phone shop.

ok.de: Zustand in der Vergangenheit, der nicht mehr gilt: used to + Grundform (nicht would).
ok.en: A past state that no longer holds: used to + base form (not would).

wrong.de: there use to gibt es in der Aussage nicht; es heißt used to.
wrong.en: there use to does not exist in a statement; it is used to.

wrong.de: would gilt nicht für Zustände wie „es gab ein Café“; hier steht used to.
wrong.en: would does not work for states like “there was a café”; here used to is needed.

wrong.de: there did to be gibt es nicht.
wrong.en: there did to be does not exist.

items.text: I was wondering ___ it would be possible to reschedule our call to Thursday, because of a customer visit.

ok.de: Weiche Bitte: I was wondering if/whether + Satz.
ok.en: A soft request: I was wondering if/whether + clause.

wrong.de: wondering that passt nicht vor einer Frage nach Möglichkeit.
wrong.en: wondering that does not fit before a question about possibility.

wrong.de: wondering when fragt nach der Zeit; hier geht es um ja oder nein.
wrong.en: wondering when asks about time; this is a yes/no question.

wrong.de: wondering what braucht eine offene Frage mit einem Fragewort als Teil.
wrong.en: wondering what needs an open question with a question word as part.

items.text: If it ___ up to me, I would choose the cheaper option, but the board makes the final decision.

ok.de: Unwirkliche Annahme: if + were/was …, would + Grundform.
ok.en: An unreal assumption: if + were/was …, would + base form.

wrong.de: if it is up to me wäre eine reale Möglichkeit; zu would passt die unwirkliche Form.
wrong.en: if it is up to me would be a real possibility; with would the unreal form fits.

wrong.de: if it be up to me ist veraltet.
wrong.en: if it be up to me is archaic.

wrong.de: would steht im Hauptsatz, nicht im if-Satz.
wrong.en: would belongs in the main clause, not the if-clause.

items.text: I would have called you earlier if I ___ known that the meeting had been cancelled until this morning.

ok.de: Dritte Bedingung: if + Past Perfect (had known), would have + Partizip.
ok.en: Third conditional: if + past perfect (had known), would have + participle.

wrong.de: if I have known passt nicht zu would have; hier braucht der if-Satz had known.
wrong.en: if I have known does not fit would have; the if-clause needs had known.

wrong.de: would steht im Hauptsatz, nicht nach if.
wrong.en: would belongs in the main clause, not after if.

wrong.de: if I did known ist falsch.
wrong.en: if I did known is wrong.
